entry.title: Claude Code › Releases & changelog: Claude Code 2.1.332 release highlights (unofficial changelog)
entry.summary: 36-second animated release card (watched): 2.1.332 with 150 CLI changes and 1 prompt change; highlights: confirmation by default for risky or destructive actions, and MCP-hosted skills (beta) shown as server:skill in the / menu. Details in the thread. • New PreSkillShellCommand hook can block a skill's inline shell: 2.1.332 adds a PreSkillShellCommand hook event that can refuse a skill or command's inline shell commands as it loads. On 2.1.331 and older, a settings file that names this hook opens a dialog at start. • /permissions now rejects rules that would be skipped: In 2.1.332, /permissions refuses a rule that would be ignored at the next start, such as rm -rf with no tool name, and shows why, so check your rules include the tool name. • Self-hosted runners: OAuth tokens can now start with oat02-: On self-hosted runners, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN's prefix can now end in oat02- as well as oat01-. Update proxy rules and log scrubbers that match oat01-, and mask the whole value. • 0:15 2.1.332 asks before risky or destructive actions again: Claude Code 2.1.332 (150 CLI changes, 1 system prompt change) defaults to confirmation for risky or destructive actions. The new "execute with care" prompt rule has Claude judge reversibility and blast radius: local, reversible steps go ahead, while destructive, hard-to-undo, shared-state or third-party upload actions get a confirmation request (with extra git status/stash checks). This reverses the 2.1.331 change. • 0:21 Skills served by MCP servers show up as server:skill: From 2.1.332, skills hosted on MCP servers (beta) appear in the / menu as server:skill; your other skills keep their names. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeCodeLog/status/2125406441796206946)

entry.title: Subagents, skills & plugins › Plugins, MCP & marketplace: MCP elicitations in Claude Code
entry.summary: • Use MCP elicitations instead of letting the model ask questions: With MCP elicitation, the server sends a JSON Schema and the host renders it as an interactive form, returning structured data straight to the server. That builds structured workflows and saves tokens compared with having the LLM collect the information from the user. • Elicitation forms in Claude Code: When an MCP server requests information, Claude Code renders an interactive form from the server's JSON Schema. In the example the server asks you to pick a component type and category before the tool call continues. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2125368426596065592)

entry.title: Claude Code › PR review & shipping: A practical guide to shipping with Claude Code (/code-review, /ship, /steward, Claude Ship)
entry.summary: • Run /code-review before you push: /code-review checks your branch's commits and uncommitted changes for correctness bugs. Variants: /code-review high 1234 (PR 1234 at high effort), --fix (apply findings to the working tree), --comment 1234 (post findings on the PR), ultra (deeper review in the cloud; needs a claude.ai login and can be billed separately). Effort runs low to max and Claude remembers the last level. Commit before --fix in a background review: /rewind may not catch those edits. • Check git status before /ship: If there's no PR yet, /ship commits pending changes as if you ran git add -A (respecting .gitignore), pushes, opens the PR as you, reviews it and fixes valid findings. It won't commit secret-looking files or rule files (CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, .claude/, .github/), and in a public repo it commits nothing, so commit those yourself. Options: /ship high, /ship 41 (PR #41), /ship +my-lint-bot (also read that bot's comments), /ship stop. • What the /ship watch needs to keep running: The watch runs as you on your machine and quota for up to seven days: keep the session open and the machine awake, run gh auth login first, and it only watches PRs you opened. Outside auto mode it stops at every prompt; it won't run in bypass-permissions mode, and on Windows it doesn't start. Give it its own checkout (use a worktree for your next task). A PreToolUse or PermissionRequest hook on Bash in the repo's .claude/settings.json prevents the watch. • Only run the watch on repos where you trust every merger: The watch merges the base branch and runs your tests, so anyone who can land changes on the base branch can run commands on your machine. Claude won't merge or force-push, and its commits skip rule files, but git hooks don't run on its commits, so put required checks in CI and branch rules. Run /ship terms before your first use. • /steward: see an existing PR through without re-reviewing: Check out the branch and run /steward 41 (or plain /steward for the current branch's PR) to run only the watch: fix failing checks, resolve conflicts and answer comments, with no review first. Stop it with /steward stop or /ship stop; one watch per session. Good fits are PRs with red checks or stuck in conflict loops, not ones in a design debate. Claude pushes at most 3 times per issue, then reports and escalates. • Turn repeated feedback into the right file: Code conventions go in CLAUDE.md (read by Claude Code, local /code-review, Code Review and PR Steward). PR review rules go in REVIEW.md (Code Review and PR Steward only, not local /code-review). How to start and exercise the app goes in .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md. How PRs should be looked after goes in .claude/skills/steward/SKILL.md. The team's bar: a pattern must repeat on at least 2 PRs before it becomes a rule. • Keep the steward skill out of the / menu: In .claude/skills/steward/SKILL.md, set user-invocable: false and disable-model-invocation: true so the house rules stay out of the / menu and out of skills Claude picks on its own. The local watch reads it from your working directory; PR Steward reads it from the default branch, so review edits to it like CI changes. • Start Claude Approvals in observe mode and keep the advisory line: Claude Approvals reads .claude/approvals.yml from the default branch. Start with mode: observe so it only reports what it would decide, and keep advisory: [claude/code_review] in rules: once a policy is on the default branch, Code Review only runs automatically on PRs matching a rule that names it. After the watch merges the base branch, the PR author should comment @claude approve. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2125365668463993091)

entry.title: Claude API & platform › Auth & billing: Claude Platform OAuth: Step-by-step Setup Guide
entry.summary: • Claude Platform OAuth: let customers pay for their own usage: With Claude Platform OAuth (beta, Linked Billing), a customer links their Claude Console organization to your app once and sets a monthly spend limit; Claude calls they start in your app are then billed to their organization. It is not sign-in with a Claude.ai plan: Pro or Max can't be linked, the org needs API billing (prepaid credits or invoice), and the person linking needs the Admin or Billing role. There is no client secret. • Test OAuth with a second account and test users: Create the app under Organization → Customers → OAuth apps (connection type organization_shared). The org that owns the app can't link it, so test with a second Claude account using a different email and its own Console org with prepaid credits. In Testing mode only listed test users can link (max USD 50/month each); add them and your callback URL on the Settings tab (http://localhost works). Publishing needs a DNS record and an Anthropic review. • Enable both billing:attribution and offline_access: Turn on both the billing:attribution and offline_access permissions for the OAuth app. With offline_access off, the authorization request fails with invalid_scope, and you also don't get the long-lived token that keeps access without asking the customer to approve again. • Use an issuer with inline keys instead of a cloud identity provider: You don't need AWS, GCP, Okta or similar for workload identity: under Keys → Workload identity → Issuers, register an issuer with inline keys (the URL is just a name and doesn't need to exist) and paste your public key. The key editor rejects the usual {"keys": [...]} format; paste only the array. Then in the app's Client authentication pick that issuer, a subject and the audience https://auth.claude.com. If you sign in Node, use ECDSA signatures in ieee-p1363 format or you get jwt_signature_invalid. • Set the default workspace before anyone links: Billed calls need a service account (Keys → Service accounts) plus a federation rule on the same issuer with the audience https://api.anthropic.com. Choose it as the Operator service account, then set "Default workspace for platform auth mode OAuth tokens" right below it. Without that field the last link step fails with unauthorized_client, and since the customer's code lasts only 5 minutes you lose a whole approval round. • OAuth backend rules: rotate refresh tokens, bind state: Save the newest refresh token every time because it rotates on each use. Check that the returned state is yours and bind it to the browser that started the flow (for example with an HttpOnly cookie). Before approval a billed call returns 403 user_profile_billing_not_authorized, a handy check. Batches and billable code execution aren't supported, and the customer's ZDR or BAA doesn't cover these calls. Customers can revoke from Keys → Linked platforms. • A skill that walks Claude through Linked Billing setup: @dani_avila7 built a Claude Platform OAuth skill that walks Claude through integrating Linked Billing into your app. Install it and ask Claude to set up Linked Billing; with the Chrome extension, Claude can ask for browser access to help fill out the Console steps. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2124967784291377195)

entry.summary: 46-second animated demo (watched), labeled an illustrative example: typing /ship opens and reviews a PR, applies a review fix, then keeps watching the PR, fixing a failed check and answering a review comment until it is ready; merging is left to you. • Claude Ship vs. the /ship skill: There are two pieces: Claude Ship (beta) for Team and Enterprise, which you turn on in settings and which can review PRs, work on fixes and approve the ones your team's policy allows; and the /ship skill, which anyone can use and which ships with the latest Claude Code version. • 0:09 Type /ship to open, review and watch a pull request: In Claude Code, type /ship to open a pull request if there is none, review it in the session, then keep watching it. entry.title: Claude Code › Hooks & guardrails: dependency-cooldown: a must-have Claude Code setting
entry.summary: • dependency-cooldown setting blocks brand-new packages: The dependency-cooldown setting for Claude Code blocks package versions published less than 7 days ago from being installed through npm, pnpm or uv. It reduces the risk of supply chain attacks, protects against slopsquatting, and requires your permission if Claude tries. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2124325975076823188)

entry.title: Subagents, skills & plugins › Skills: vulnerability-scanner skill
entry.summary: • vulnerability-scanner skill for security reviews: The vulnerability-scanner skill reviews your code for security vulnerabilities, including AI agents and MCP servers. It maps the attack surface and trust boundaries, detects prompt injection and insecure agent tools, checks for exposed secrets and vulnerable dependencies, reviews MCP servers, skills, hooks and CLAUDE.md files, flags OWASP and CI/CD risks, verifies findings to cut false positives, and reports each issue with Attack, Impact and Fix. It is read-only and never modifies your code. In his tests it activated automatically in 7/7 runs with 0 false positives across 7 decoys. Install: `npx claude-code-templates@latest --skill security/vulnerability-scanner`. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2124014299483873352)

entry.title: Claude Code › Commands & settings: Claude Code 2.1.330 release highlights (unofficial changelog)
entry.summary: 36-second animated release card (watched): it announces 2.1.330 with 142 CLI changes and 1 prompt change, and repeats the two highlights, the confirm-before-risky-actions policy and Enterprise Admin Console sign-in. The full changelog and system prompt notes are in the thread. • Sign in to an Enterprise Admin Console org: Claude Code 2.1.330 can sign in to organizations managed in Anthropic's Enterprise Admin Console: after `claude auth login`, Claude Code applies the organization's settings and uses its cloud provider or gateway. • easel draws charts; turn it off in /config: 2.1.330 adds easel, a built-in mod that draws charts when asked and under MCP metrics results (Pro, Max and, where available, Team and Enterprise, on macOS and Linux). Turn automatic charts off in `/config`. • Print the full sign-in link: Set `CLAUDE_CODE_FULL_SIGN_IN_LINK=1` (2.1.330) to print the full sign-in link, if the short one shows an error or a script reads values from it. • Claude now asks before destructive actions: Claude Code 2.1.330 adds a confirm-before-risky-actions policy. The system prompt now has a “measure twice, cut once” rule: Claude weighs reversibility and blast radius and asks for confirmation before destructive, hard-to-reverse, shared-state or public actions such as rm -rf, reset --hard, force-push, PR comments, Slack/email and third-party uploads, including git status/stash checks. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeCodeLog/status/2123913205575496028)

entry.title: Subagents, skills & plugins › Plugins, MCP & marketplace: MCP Events is here
entry.summary: • MCP Events: agents that react without a prompt: With MCP Events, AI agents can subscribe to external events and react without waiting for a user prompt, for example starting a code review and running tests when a new PR arrives in a GitHub repository. It supports three delivery modes: Poll, Push and Webhook. In Poll mode the client discovers available events, checks the server, waits and checks again; when an event arrives it is passed to the agent runtime. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2123896682907664610)

entry.title: Claude Code › Hooks & guardrails: Lydia Hallie: Rethinking Claude Code Best Practices
entry.summary: @lydiahallie's talk "Rethinking Claude Code Best Practices": with newer models you can step out of the loop. Five areas: lighter CLAUDE.md steering, Auto mode instead of manual approvals, deny rules, sandboxing and cloud sessions for safety, verification through prompts, hooks and CI, and orchestrating many sessions with Claude Code projects. • 2:45 Move from Manual to Auto permission mode: With newer models, switch the permission mode from Manual to Auto: they read intent and your codebase well enough that you don't need to approve every command or steer mid-session. • 3:37 Cut generic warnings from CLAUDE.md: Remove generic instructions such as "Think hard and be thorough." or "IMPORTANT: always use the auth helper" from CLAUDE.md. Newer models don't need them, and clutter like this can derail them. • 3:42 Keep CLAUDE.md to what Claude can't infer: Limit CLAUDE.md to context Claude can't see or work out from the code, for example that a legacy directory is still used by the mobile apps. • 3:56 Audit your instructions with /doctor prompt-audit: Run `/doctor prompt-audit` to check your CLAUDE.md and skills for instructions the new model no longer needs. • 4:48 Describe Auto mode's trust boundaries in plain English: In `.claude/settings.json`, an `autoMode` block takes plain-English lists: `environment` (e.g. "Trusted cloud buckets: s3://acme-staging"), `allow` ("Deploying to staging is allowed") and `hard_deny` ("Never send code to third-party APIs"), each starting with `"$defaults"`. • 6:04 Hard-block commands with deny rules: Add a command to `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.json`, e.g. `"Bash(git reset --hard *)"`, to block it in the harness before the Auto mode classifier ever sees it. • 6:32 Rule of thumb for what to deny: If Claude could make a mistake you can take back (like git edits), leave it to the model. If you can't take it back (deleting something for good, exposing a secret, sending data outside), make it a deny rule. • 6:58 Deny reads of secrets: Add deny rules like `"Read(./.env)"` and `"Read(~/.ssh/**)"` so a compromised dependency can't trick Claude into reading or leaking your secrets. • 8:17 Turn on the shell sandbox: Add `"sandbox": { "enabled": true }` to `.claude/settings.json` to sandbox shell commands at the OS level, limiting which files, folders and hosts a command like `npm test` and its child processes can reach. • 9:30 Run long tasks in a cloud session: Cloud sessions run on a fresh, isolated machine with your repo, keep going with your laptop closed, and keep local secrets such as `.env`, `~/.ssh` and GitHub tokens out of reach. • 9:51 Give cloud sessions only the network and secrets they need: Configure Network access with allowed domains (e.g. `api.example.com`) and hand over API keys through Network secrets, instead of exposing your local environment. • 12:06 Ask Claude to prove its work: Prompt for verifiable steps, for example "Split it into tasks, each with its own test." and "Show me the test output." • 12:24 Run checks from lifecycle hooks: Use hooks to verify automatically: `PostToolUse` to lint after every edit, `TaskCompleted` to run a task's tests, and `Stop` to run the full suite at the end. • 13:02 Fail checks with exit 2, not exit 1: Make your check scripts exit with code 2 on failure. Exit 1, the common default, gets marked as completed; exit 2 sends Claude back to fix it. • 14:14 Let CI failures loop back to Claude: With CI auto-fix, a failed PR check goes back to Claude, which fixes it without you stepping in. • 14:26 Auto-merge once checks pass: Turn on "Merge when ready" so PRs merge automatically after their checks pass, so you don't have to hand-review small, safe changes. • 14:40 Match review effort to risk: Let agents do the first review on every PR, then require no humans for small changes (typos, lint fixes), one person for most changes, and several for the riskiest. • 15:28 Let a project orchestrate the sessions: Claude Code projects (in beta) take an overall goal; an orchestrator splits the work, starts worker sessions and manages their context, so you don't have to juggle sessions yourself. • 15:54 Fable to orchestrate, Opus 5.5 to code: In a project, put a reasoning model like Fable on the orchestrator (deciding tasks, judging results) and Opus 5.5 on the worker threads that write the code. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vlfCjWuv4es)

entry.title: Claude API & platform › Model upgrades: How Anthropic launches new models on the API (ClaudeDevs video)
entry.summary: @dejno and @luccasiau on keeping API costs down in agentic work: prompt caching across turns, what breaks the cache, and using an evals harness to compare models and settings on cost. • Rethink your harness when you upgrade models: When you upgrade to a new model, rethink your harness and measure cost per task. That is the topic of this ClaudeDevs video with @dejno and @luccasiau, who also explain how Anthropic launches new models on its API. • 0:08 Lean on prompt caching in agent loops: In agentic turns, follow-up requests that repeat or append to the first request reuse cached blocks, which cuts cost. • 0:24 Don't change the system prompt or effort mid-conversation: Changing the system prompt or the effort setting partway through a conversation breaks prompt caching. • 0:42 Use an evals harness when switching models: Build and tune an evals harness so that when you switch models or adjust settings such as thinking, you can confirm you get the same outcome on a better cost curve. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2120962481225146636)

entry.title: Subagents, skills & plugins › Subagents: api-security-audit subagent
entry.summary: • api-security-audit subagent: Run the API Security Audit subagent on your REST API: it reviews authentication and JWT vulnerabilities, authorization flaws and privilege escalation, SQL/NoSQL injection, sensitive data exposure, and OWASP API Top 10 and rate limiting, then suggests fixes with code examples. Install: `npx claude-code-templates@latest --agent security/api-security-audit`. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2123268852196786589)

entry.title: Claude Code › Releases & changelog: Claude Code 2.1.328 release highlights (unofficial changelog)
entry.summary: • Auto mode on clouds and gateways: Claude Code 2.1.328 adds auto mode for Opus/Sonnet 4.6 on clouds and gateways, letting sessions skip permission prompts. It also warns that cloud sessions may hold or drop messages when permission prompts are skipped. • onFailure: block for mcp_tool hooks: 2.1.328 added `onFailure: block` for mcp_tool hooks, so a failed hook call blocks the action instead of allowing a partial run. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeCodeLog/status/2123226990551445634)

entry.title: Subagents, skills & plugins › Skills: Check a skill's compatibility across harnesses
entry.summary: • Check a skill's compatibility across harnesses: A skill loading successfully doesn't mean it works as intended across agents. aitmpl.com now runs NVIDIA SkillEvaluator to check a skill against six harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw) and shows issues and suggested fixes for each; open any skill and select the Compatibility tab. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2123223560579633625)

entry.title: Claude API & platform › Auth & billing: Claude Platform OAuth and Linked Billing for agent platforms
entry.summary: • Claude Platform OAuth instead of API keys: With Claude Platform OAuth, users connect their Claude organization to your app instead of sharing API keys. Usage is billed to the customer's organization, developers choose who pays for each request, and users can set spending limits and revoke access at any time. • Use billing_policy to choose who pays: With Linked Billing, set `billing_policy` to decide per API request whether your platform or your customer pays, so you can charge for your software while users pay for their own tokens. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2123135599833964893)

entry.title: Subagents, skills & plugins › Subagents: supabase-schema-architect subagent
entry.summary: • supabase-schema-architect subagent: For Supabase projects, the supabase-schema-architect agent designs schemas, migrations, RLS policies and Storage permissions. It covers explicit grants in every migration, RLS policies with auth.uid() and proper WITH CHECK rules, security definer functions without recursive policies, column-level permissions and PostgreSQL 16 trigger/RLS execution order. Before delivering, it tests access as two different authenticated users and runs the Supabase linter. Install: `npx claude-code-templates@latest --agent database/supabase-schema-architect`. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2122937536565641711)

entry.title: Projects & cloud sessions › Long-running cloud sessions: Design long runs for surprise restarts
entry.summary: • Design long runs for surprise restarts: In Claude Projects and cloud sessions, the machine can restart without warning during hours-long processes, stopping containers, orchestrators and monitoring; completed work stays on disk but in-progress work can be lost. Make your orchestrator checkpoint after every step, resume from the last successful step, recover with a single script, check disk space and budget before each step, and alert you immediately when something stops. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2122918299600093267)

entry.title: Claude Code › Releases & changelog: Claude Code 2.1.327 release highlights (unofficial changelog)
entry.summary: • Stateful multi-step workflows: Claude Code 2.1.327 can launch agents that split complex multi-step tasks into stateful workflows. • /install-github-app asks first: In 2.1.327, `/install-github-app` asks for confirmation before modifying a repository. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeCodeLog/status/2122835481855394129)

entry.title: Claude Code › Releases & changelog: Claude Code 2.1.326 release highlights (unofficial changelog)
entry.summary: • Confirmations for destructive actions: Claude Code 2.1.326 added confirmations for risky destructive actions (git operations, deletes) to reduce accidental data loss. • Agent-team sessions open in Code Mode: In 2.1.326, agent-team sessions start in Code Mode when it is enabled. • No more SSH logouts from PID reuse: In 2.1.326, the background service no longer kills user processes on PID reuse, which had caused unexpected SSH logouts. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeCodeLog/status/2122821446602780783)

entry.title: Claude Code › Desktop, themes & simulators: Switch Claude Desktop to the Latest release channel
entry.summary: • Switch Claude Desktop to the Latest release channel: To get more frequent Claude Desktop builds on Windows and Mac, switch to the Latest release channel in Settings > Desktop app. Fixes and improvements arrive faster, but these builds can be less reliable than Stable, which stays the default. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2122821051910684824)

entry.title: Verification & security › Security programs: Anthropic's security programs for developers
entry.summary: • Anthropic's security programs for developers: Anthropic is cutting disclosure timelines for high and critical vulnerabilities from 90 to 30 days, and opening three programs: OSS Scanner (Claude scans open-source projects for vulnerabilities), Claude for Open Source (6 months of Claude Ultra free for eligible maintainers) and the Cyber Verification Program (access to Claude for legitimate security research). (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2122803331156398269)

entry.title: Claude Code › Code Mode & tool use: Try experimental Code Mode
entry.summary: • Try experimental Code Mode: Code Mode is a new, experimental way for Claude Code to work with tools: Claude writes scripts that chain your tools together, and it can answer you while long commands are still running. Opt in with `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1`. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2122801681939234950)

entry.title: Claude API & platform › Auth & billing: Linked billing (beta)
entry.summary: • Linked billing (beta): Linked billing is in beta on the Claude Platform: users of tools like Factory, Linear and Ramp can pay for Claude API usage through their own Claude Platform organization without sharing an API key. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2122751844455956760)

entry.title: Subagents, skills & plugins › Plugins, MCP & marketplace: AI Templates MCP in the Claude plugin marketplace
entry.summary: • AI Templates MCP in the Claude plugin marketplace: The AI Templates MCP in the official Claude Plugin Marketplace lets Claude search nearly 2,000 Claude Code components (agents, skills, hooks, commands, MCPs, settings, plugins), inspect their source and security scans, and generate one command that installs up to 20 of them. Tools: search_components, get_component, get_install_command, list_categories. It is remote, read-only and needs no account. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2122544936239218893)

entry.title: Verification & security › Sandboxing: The external sandbox pattern
entry.summary: • The external sandbox pattern: In the external sandbox pattern, the coding agent runs on your Mac but executes code inside a WebAssembly, QEMU or Apple Container sandbox. The write-up includes a demo for Claude Code (plus Codex and Pi). (Source: https://x.com/simonw/status/2122500307557265651)

entry.title: Verification & security › Verification: Let Claude verify its own work
entry.summary: • Let Claude verify its own work: Claude writes better code when it can verify its work, and checks that used to be expensive (tests, benchmarks, end-to-end runs) are now cheap. The Claude Code team's approach is written up on the Claude blog. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2122457608963395586)

entry.title: Claude Code › Desktop, themes & simulators: Test foldable layouts with iPhone Duo
entry.summary: • Test foldable layouts with iPhone Duo: Claude Code on desktop supports iPhone Duo in the iOS simulator (public beta). Run your app on Duo next to your conversation, and Claude can fold and unfold the device to test each layout. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2122439098740674839)

entry.title: Verification & security › Security programs: Cyber Verification Program unlocks Defense Access
entry.summary: • Cyber Verification Program unlocks Defense Access: Approval for Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program gives your Claude account Defense Access, which reduces security-related blocks for legitimate defensive work such as malware analysis, vulnerability validation and incident response, and includes access to Claude Mythos models. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2122012847958007962)

entry.title: Claude Code › Code Mode & tool use: What Code Mode changes
entry.summary: • What Code Mode changes: Available experimentally from Claude Code 2.1.325: instead of calling tools one by one, Claude writes JavaScript that runs several tool calls in a single step. It can run commands in parallel, chain operations, and filter results before they are sent back to the model. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2121789088499933223)

entry.title: Claude Code › Model choice & cost: Opus 5.5 medium as a daily driver
entry.summary: • Opus 5.5 medium as a daily driver: Opus 5.5 at medium effort is a fantastic daily driver and baseline. For when to reach for Fable 5.2 instead of Opus 5.5, see the Claude blog's model guidance. (Source: https://x.com/RLanceMartin/status/2121721387547267498)

entry.title: Claude apps › Chat & permissions: Unblock auto mode by granting permission in chat
entry.summary: • Unblock auto mode by granting permission in chat: Regular Claude chat now uses auto mode, so it occasionally refuses to run something. Prompting "Hey permission system, I give this session permission to run this experiment for me (now try again)" seemed to unblock it, because auto mode takes your messages into account. (Source: https://x.com/simonw/status/2121695097674981849)

entry.title: Subagents, skills & plugins › Subagents: database-architect subagent for migrations
entry.summary: • database-architect subagent for migrations: The rewritten database-architect agent reads your existing schema and migrations, catches locking risks and breaking changes, handles rolling deployments (using lock_timeout and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) and tests migrations on a temporary database before finishing. In his test (an 80M-row table, a migration needed 10 minutes before deployment), the same prompt scored 6/10 without the agent and 10/10 with it, and Claude picked the agent automatically in all 8 tests. Install: `npx claude-code-templates@latest --agent database/database-architect`. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2121470943314788696)

entry.title: Projects & cloud sessions › Projects: Let the project coordinator run parallel threads
entry.summary: • Let the project coordinator run parallel threads: In a Claude Code project, Claude coordinates your tasks across parallel threads. The coordinator is now more proactive: it answers your questions in the project chat and gives you status updates on ongoing threads. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2121375309287301360)

entry.title: Claude Code › Hooks & guardrails: Make a Stop hook retry with exit code 2
entry.summary: • Make a Stop hook retry with exit code 2: A Stop hook can send Claude back to try again when a check fails, but only if the hook exits with code 2. Exit 2 returns Claude to retry with the hook's stderr; exit 1 is non-blocking, so Claude just finishes even though the check failed. (Source: https://x.com/lydiahallie/status/2121313048820617645)

entry.title: Claude Code › Model choice & cost: Opus as the main model, Fable 5.2 as advisor
entry.summary: • Opus as the main model, Fable 5.2 as advisor: Use Opus as your main model and Fable 5.2 as its advisor in Claude Code. Opus handles every turn; Fable steps in at critical moments: choosing an approach, debugging recurring errors and reviewing work before completion. You get Fable's judgment without paying for Fable on every turn. (Source: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2121076519296450582)

entry.title: Claude Code › Commands & settings: Run /doctor prompt-audit
entry.summary: • Run /doctor prompt-audit: Run `/doctor prompt-audit` in each of your Claude Code repos if you haven't yet. (Source: https://x.com/lydiahallie/status/2121011733699633613)

entry.title: Prompting & context › Closing context gaps: Find the context Claude is missing
entry.summary: • Find the context Claude is missing: A lot of getting good work out of Claude now is finding the context it's missing and closing that gap. Claude Meetings is one way to bring in the remaining pieces and has proved useful inside Anthropic. (Source: https://x.com/alexalbert__/status/2120983722182988206)

entry.title: Claude apps › Meetings: Add Claude to your video calls
entry.summary: • Add Claude to your video calls: Claude Meetings adds Claude to your team's video call, where it builds docs, whiteboards and other artifacts with you while you are still talking. Rolling out in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. (Source: https://x.com/claudeai/status/2120973994191094179)

entry.title: Claude API & platform › Managed Agents: Self-host Claude Managed Agents
entry.summary: • Self-host Claude Managed Agents: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents is in private beta: host the agent harness, sandboxes and session history in your own cloud or on-premises, and choose where requests to Claude are sent. (Source: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2120938988165091693)
